opportunities.title: The 0-Day That Hacked Itself: Inside China's AI-Agent Attack on a University Server
opportunities.why_now: Reports confirm an autonomous AI agent — not a human operator — found and exploited a zero-day to seize a university server, a first-of-its-kind milestone for offensive AI.
opportunities.angle: Analysis piece breaking down what 'autonomous exploitation' actually means technically, why it changes the patch-cadence calculus, and what defenders should do differently this week.

opportunities.title: Armory Castle Is Already Inside: The VMware vCenter Zero-Day You Needed to Patch Yesterday
opportunities.why_now: A newly patched vCenter flaw was actively exploited in the wild by a Chinese APT before the fix shipped, and it's now confirmed alongside fresh Cisco/Apache espionage activity.
opportunities.angle: Breach-digest timeline: zero-day discovery → exploitation → patch → ongoing risk window, with a clear 'are you exposed' checklist for vCenter admins.

opportunities.title: PHP Just Patched Seven Critical RCEs — Here's Why 'PHP2Shell' Isn't the New Log4Shell (Yet)
opportunities.why_now: PHP shipped patches for seven critical code-execution bugs the same week PHP 8.6 tightens strictness, giving ops teams a dual patch-and-migrate headache right before the holidays.
opportunities.angle: Patch-cadence explainer: what's actually exploitable now, what's theoretical, and a prioritized patch order for teams juggling PHP, VMware, KVM, and Ruby2Shell all at once.

opportunities.title: Visa, Mastercard, Chase, JPMorgan: One Third Party, Four Household Names, Millions of Records
opportunities.why_now: Within 48 hours, four major financial brands confirmed exposure from the same third-party breach, with researchers noting the stolen data enables phishing but not direct account drains — a nuance worth correcting before panic spreads.
opportunities.angle: Breach-digest roundup clarifying exactly what was and wasn't stolen, why 'can't drain your account' still means 'expect targeted phishing,' and what card-holders should actually do.

opportunities.title: SonicWall Just Told Gen 6 Firewall Owners: No More Patches, Even for Critical Flaws
opportunities.why_now: SonicWall's end-of-life announcement for Gen 6 firewalls means any future critical CVE on that hardware is now permanently unpatched — a slow-motion breach waiting to happen for anyone still running it.
opportunities.angle: Inevitable-breach framing: a countdown piece on orphaned hardware, who's still exposed, and a migration deadline checklist for admins.
